```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```


```{python}
followers = pl.read_csv("https://byuidatascience.github.io/DS250-Course-Polars/Data/social_media_followers.csv")
```


GOAL: Create new columns


Let's put the values in terms of millions


```{python}
# Does not work.
# followers["instagram"] = followers["instagram"] / 1000000
```


Instead use the with.columns() command.

```{python}
followers.with_columns(pl.col("instagram") / 1000000)
```



with_columns() is just SYNTACTIC SUGAR for select()

```{python}
followers.select(pl.col("instagram") / 1000000, pl.all().exclude("instagram"))
```



If we want to give the column a new name, there are 2 ways:

- assign it a name with an =
- with the alias() method



```{python}
# assign new name with =
followers.with_columns(insta_mill = pl.col("instagram") / 1000000).head(5)
```



```{python}
# Use the alias
followers.with_columns((pl.col("instagram") / 1000000).alias("insta_mill")).head(5)
```




Let's do the transformation to all of the columns, with an end to calculate the relative frequency for each artist. (aka what % of their followers comes from each platform)



```{python}
followers.with_columns(
    pl.col("instagram") / 1000000,
    pl.col("youtube") / 1000000,
    pl.col("facebook") / 1000000,
    pl.col("twitter") / 1000000,
).with_columns(
    total = pl.col("instagram") + pl.col("youtube") + pl.col("facebook") + pl.col("twitter")
).with_columns(
    insta_perc = (pl.col("instagram") / pl.col("total")),
    you_perc = (pl.col("youtube") / pl.col("total")),
    face_perc = (pl.col("facebook") / pl.col("total")),
    twit_perc = (pl.col("twitter") / pl.col("total")),
).head(5)
```


Let's use expression expansion to reduce the amount of typing.


```{python}
followers.with_columns(
    pl.col(["instagram", "youtube", "facebook", "twitter"]) / 1000000
).with_columns(
    total = pl.col("instagram") + pl.col("youtube") + pl.col("facebook") + pl.col("twitter")
).with_columns(
    (
        pl.col([
            "instagram", 
            "youtube", 
            "facebook", 
            "twitter"
        ]) / pl.col("total")
    ).name.suffix("_perc")
).head()
```



```{python}
df = (
    followers.with_columns(
        pl.col(["instagram", "youtube", "facebook", "twitter"]) / 1000000
    ).with_columns(
        # total = pl.col("instagram") + pl.col("youtube") + pl.col("facebook") + pl.col("twitter")
        # total = pl.sum_horizontal(pl.all().exclude("id"))
        total = pl.sum_horizontal(pl.col(pl.Float64))
    ).with_columns(
        (
            pl.col([
                "instagram", 
                "youtube", 
                "facebook", 
                "twitter"
            ]) / pl.col("total")
        ).name.suffix("_perc")
    ).sort("instagram_perc", descending=True)
)
```



```{python}
(
    ggplot(data=df, mapping=aes(x="instagram_perc", y="id"))
    + geom_bar(stat="identity")
)
```
